title: Prepared Statements
summary: Prepared statements send SQL structure and data separately so user input cannot change query meaning — the core defense against SQL injection in PHP.
objectives: Prepare once, execute many with bound values
Contrast safe binding with string concatenation

content.md: An attacker should not be able to turn a login lookup into `OR 1=1`. Placeholders (`?` or `:email`) keep their input in the **data channel** only.

content.code:
<?php
$stmt = $pdo->prepare('SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = ? LIMIT 1');
$stmt->execute([$email]);
$user = $stmt->fetch();

content.md: Never concatenate: "SELECT ... WHERE id = " . $_GET["id"]. Always bind parameters.
